findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks sender
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (a 500) if the Integration exists without a `sender` entry. Integrations created before the webhook stored the sender, or when `state.get("sender")` was falsy, have no such key. Use `.get` chains and fail with the error page instead.

findings.title: User validation only applies when an Integration already exists
findings.body: When no Integration exists (`Integration.DoesNotExist` at line 481), the pipeline proceeds via `next_step()` without comparing the authenticated GitHub user to the installer. The check only runs for an existing Integration with no OrganizationIntegration. A first-time install by someone other than the installing GitHub user is therefore not validated, which weakens the security fix.

findings.title: Token exchange and user lookup lack error handling
findings.body: `safe_urlopen` is outside the try block, so network errors or timeouts raise 500s. `get_user_info` can also raise on an API error. Both should be caught and turned into the error page. The `state` parameter is also interpolated into the redirect URL without URL-encoding.

findings.title: Non-constant-time comparison and OAuth state reuse
findings.body: The `state` comparison uses plain `!=`, and the code is not tied to the pipeline beyond the signature. The OAuth step also runs again whenever `state` is in the query. A later `installation_id`-only request skips it, so the bound `github_authenticated_user` is never re-verified. Consider `constant_time_compare`.

findings.title: Brittle index into responses.calls
findings.body: `responses.calls[2]` depends on the exact number and order of HTTP calls made by the new OAuth step. Any change to those calls will silently check the wrong request. Find the call by URL instead.
